functions.name: hook_command
functions.behavior: Builds the shell command string a single hook runs: the shell-quoted absolute path to the agent-hook executable, then a space, agent, space, action. Python: `f"{shlex.quote(HOOK)} {agent} {action}"`. Only HOOK is quoted; agent/action are interpolated raw (they are trusted manifest tokens). HOOK itself is the realpath-resolved path to agent-hook.sh (in the Rust port, the resolved path/invocation of the hook subcommand, see `hook` module dep).
edge_cases: Quoting MUST match Python shlex.quote exactly: return the string unquoted when it matches the safe set [A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+, otherwise wrap in single quotes and replace each embedded single quote with the 4-char sequence '\''. Empty string -> '' (two single quotes).
agent and action are NOT quoted; they contain only word chars in the manifest, but the port must interpolate them verbatim (a space in action would break parity, matching Python's current behavior).

HOOK is derived from realpath of the script dir + /agent-hook.sh; symlinks are resolved. Port must resolve the hook path the same stable way so the emitted command string is deterministic across runs.

functions.name: groups
functions.behavior: Normalizes one manifest event value into a list of (optional matcher, actions) groups. Two accepted shapes: (a) a JSON array of action strings -> single group [(None, actions)]; (b) a JSON array of objects {matcher?, actions} -> one group per object, matcher = object.get('matcher') (None if absent). Detection is `value && isinstance(value[0], dict)`.
edge_cases: Empty array value -> the `value && ...` guard is false, so returns [(None, [])] (a single no-matcher group with an empty action list). For the claude renderer this yields a group with an empty hooks array; the manifest never triggers this but the port must reproduce it, not skip it.
Object form with a missing 'actions' key is a hard error in Python (KeyError). Port should error (not default to empty) to preserve fail-loud parity.
Detection keys only on the first element's type; a mixed array (string then object) would be treated as string-form. Preserve.
matcher present but null in JSON is treated as None (no matcher emitted).

functions.name: is_wrangler_command
functions.behavior: Returns whether a hook command string belongs to this agent's wrangler hooks. Python uses `re.search(rf"\bagent-hook\.sh\b.*\b{re.escape(agent)}\b", cmd)`: the literal token agent-hook.sh (word-bounded) followed by anything, followed by the word-bounded agent name. Used to identify wrangler's own groups for in-place replacement/upgrade regardless of the exact path form previously written (e.g. README's ~/.tmux/... path).
edge_cases: Regex is deliberately loose (substring/word-boundary), NOT an exact command match, so entries written by an older release with a different absolute path are still recognised and upgraded in place. Do not tighten to an exact-string compare.
`.` in the regex is default (does not match newline); cmd is always a single line so this is moot, but keep single-line semantics.
agent must be regex-escaped before interpolation (re.escape). In the port, escape the agent literal or use a non-regex two-substring check that reproduces the word-boundary semantics.

Word boundaries matter: 'agent-hook.sh' must not match inside a longer token; keep \b anchors. The literal `agent-hook.sh` in the Rust port must track whatever the hook binary/command is actually named (cross-module: `hook`).

functions.name: atomic_write
functions.signature: fn atomic_write(path: &Path, text: &str, mode: u32) -> io::Result<()>
functions.behavior: Atomically replaces path's contents: makedirs(parent, exist_ok), create a temp file in the SAME directory (mkstemp), write text, chmod temp to `mode`, os.replace(temp, path) (atomic rename). On any error, unlink the temp file and re-raise.
functions.side_effects: Filesystem: creates parent dirs, writes+renames a temp file, sets file permissions. Leaves no temp file behind on failure.
edge_cases: Temp file MUST be created in the same directory as the target so os.replace is a same-filesystem atomic rename (a cross-fs /tmp temp would fail EXDEV). Preserve.
chmod is applied to the temp file BEFORE the rename, so the final file lands with `mode` (umask does not apply to the final mode).
Cleanup swallows OSError on the temp unlink (best-effort). Reproduce: ignore errors when removing the temp on the failure path.
Parent directory creation uses exist_ok semantics (no error if it already exists).

functions.name: dumps
functions.behavior: Serializes a JSON value with `json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n"`: 2-space indentation, a trailing newline appended, key order preserved as in the value.
edge_cases: Python json.dumps defaults to ensure_ascii=True: all non-ASCII characters are emitted as \uXXXX escapes. serde_json's pretty printer does NOT escape non-ASCII by default — the port MUST force ASCII escaping to match byte-for-byte, or config diffs will differ.
Exactly ONE trailing newline is appended (json.dumps itself emits none). No trailing whitespace on any line; indent is 2 spaces; item separator with indent is ',' and key separator ': '.
Key/object ordering follows insertion order — the port must use an order-preserving map (e.g. serde_json with preserve_order / IndexMap) so re-installs produce identical output and minimal diffs.
Empty object serializes as `{}` and empty array as `[]` (no inner spaces), matching Python.

functions.name: install_claude
functions.signature: fn install_claude(agent: &str, spec: &AgentSpec, hook_path: &Path, uninstall: bool) -> Result<()>
functions.behavior: Merges (install) or strips (uninstall) wrangler's hook groups inside a SHARED settings.json (default ~/.claude/settings.json, from spec.target, tilde-expanded). Reads existing JSON (or {} if missing/blank), takes data['hooks'] (or {} if absent/non-dict). For each (event, value) in spec.events: keeps existing groups for that event EXCEPT any group whose hooks contain a wrangler command (is_wrangler_command over each hook's 'command'); on install, appends wrangler's own groups built from groups(value): each group = {'hooks': [{'type':'command','command': hook_command(agent, action)} for action in actions]}, with {'matcher': m, ...} prepended when the group has a matcher. Empty kept -> remove the event key; empty hooks -> remove the 'hooks' key from data. Writes a .wrangler.bak backup of the pre-existing file, then atomic_write with dumps(data). Prints 'agent: Installed into <path>' / 'Uninstalled from <path>'.
functions.side_effects: Filesystem: reads target; if it exists, copies it to <target>.wrangler.bak (copy2, preserving metadata) EVERY run; atomically rewrites target. Stdout: one status line.
edge_cases: Missing file OR blank/whitespace-only file -> data = {} (text.strip() falsy).
Top-level JSON not an object -> hard error `SystemExit(f'{path}: expected a JSON object at the top level')`. Preserve the fail-loud behavior and message shape.
data['hooks'] present but not a dict (e.g. a list) -> silently replaced with {}, discarding it. Preserve.
A user's existing group is dropped IN FULL if ANY hook inside it matches is_wrangler_command (mixed user+wrangler group would lose the user hooks). Preserve this all-or-nothing group filtering.
Wrangler groups are appended AFTER surviving user groups, in manifest groups() order; event iteration follows spec.events insertion order (JSON object order). Order must be preserved for idempotency.

claude group shape: actions of one manifest group collapse into a single group's 'hooks' array; matcher, when present, is the FIRST key ({'matcher':..., **group} => matcher before hooks). Preserve key order.

uninstall path still filters+rewrites and still writes the .wrangler.bak backup when the file exists; it just does not append. An uninstall on a file with no wrangler hooks still rewrites (potentially reordering via pop) and re-backs-up.
Backup is overwritten on every invocation while target exists (not one-time). Preserve.
File mode: existing target -> st_mode & 0o777 preserved; new target -> 0o600 (may hold secrets, private default).
After merge, if the whole hooks map is empty -> the 'hooks' key is removed from data (not left as {}).
Idempotent: install twice reproduces byte-identical output (relies on stable quoting + ordered JSON).

functions.name: install_copilot
functions.signature: fn install_copilot(agent: &str, spec: &AgentSpec, hook_path: &Path, uninstall: bool) -> Result<()>
functions.behavior: Writes (install) or deletes (uninstall) a DEDICATED file wrangler owns outright (default ~/.copilot/hooks/wrangler.json, from spec.target). Uninstall: unlink the file; print 'Removed <path>' or, if absent, 'Nothing to remove at <path>'. Install: build doc = {'version': 1, 'hooks': {event: [ {'type':'command', matcher?, 'bash': hook_command(agent, action)} for (matcher, actions) in groups(value) for action in actions ] for (event, value) in spec.events}} and atomic_write dumps(doc). Print 'Installed into <path>'.
functions.side_effects: Filesystem: unlink (uninstall) or atomic rewrite (install). Stdout: one status line. No backup (owned file).
edge_cases: copilot shape FLATTENS: unlike claude, every (matcher, action) pair becomes its OWN hook entry {type, matcher?, bash}; a group's actions are NOT nested under a shared 'hooks' array. Matcher is repeated on each flattened entry and included only when non-None. Preserve.
Key order within each entry: 'type', then optional 'matcher', then 'bash' ({'type':'command', **matcher_or_empty, 'bash':...}).
'bash' key (not 'command') carries the shell command for copilot; 'version': 1 wraps the doc.
Uninstall distinguishes FileNotFoundError to print 'Nothing to remove' vs 'Removed'. Preserve both messages.
File mode: existing file -> st_mode & 0o777 preserved; new file -> 0o644 (world-readable default, unlike claude's 0o600).
No .wrangler.bak backup is written for copilot (the file is wrangler-owned).

functions.name: load_manifest
functions.signature: fn load_manifest(path: &Path) -> Result<Manifest>  // Manifest = ordered map<String, AgentSpec>; AgentSpec { target: String, format: String, events: OrderedMap<String, EventValue> }
functions.behavior: Loads scripts/hooks-manifest.json (path derived from the executable/script dir). Each top-level key is an agent name; each value has target, format ('claude'|'copilot'), and events (event-name -> EventValue, where EventValue is either [String] or [{matcher?, actions:[String]}]).
edge_cases: Manifest key iteration order (agent order for the 'all' selector) and events insertion order MUST be preserved — use ordered deserialization.
EventValue is a union type; deserialize permissively (array-of-strings OR array-of-objects) and let groups() interpret it, mirroring the runtime shape detection rather than a rigid schema.
In the port the manifest may be embedded at compile time or shipped as a data file; either way the byte content and ordering must match scripts/hooks-manifest.json.

functions.name: install_hooks_main
functions.behavior: CLI entry for the installer. Parses argv: '--uninstall' sets uninstall; '-h'/'--help' prints the module docstring and returns 0; one of 'all'|'claude'|'copilot' sets the selector (LAST such arg wins, default 'all'); any other arg prints 'unknown argument: <arg>' + docstring to stderr and returns 2. Loads the manifest. agents = all manifest keys (selector 'all') else [selector]. For each agent: look up spec; if absent print 'agent: not in manifest, skipping' to stderr and continue; else dispatch FORMATS[spec.format] (claude|copilot). Returns 0 on success.
functions.side_effects: Delegates to install_claude/install_copilot (filesystem writes, stdout); stderr for errors/skips.
edge_cases: Selector precedence: later positional wins (e.g. `claude all` -> 'all'); flags and selector can be interleaved in any order.
Unknown positional arg -> exit code 2 with message + full docstring on stderr.
-h/--help short-circuits with exit 0 after printing the docstring (matches Python; help wins even if combined with other args since it returns immediately in the loop).
Selector naming an agent not in the manifest (only possible via 'claude'/'copilot' when the manifest lacks it) -> stderr 'not in manifest, skipping', continue, overall return 0.
spec.format not in FORMATS -> Python raises KeyError (unhandled crash). Port MUST decide: reproduce a hard error, or improve to a clean message; note this is currently an unguarded crash.
run backgrounded (see init) so a nonzero exit / crash on tmux load is invisible; keep failures non-fatal to plugin load.

functions.name: init
functions.behavior: Port of wrangler.tmux (TPM entry point). Reads @wrangler-key (default 'Tab') and binds it (prefix table) to run the toggle command. Reads @wrangler-focus-key (default 'a') and binds it to run the focus command. If @wrangler-auto-install-hooks is on|1|yes|true, runs the installer BACKGROUNDED. Installs global hooks after-new-window and after-break-pane to run `spawn --if-active`. Unsets the legacy global hook session-window-changed. Patches automatic-rename-format: read it (-gv), and unless it already contains the substring '@wrangler_sidebar', wrap it as `#{?#{@wrangler_sidebar},#{window_name},<fmt>}` so focusing the sidebar pane does not rename the window to the sidebar's command.
functions.side_effects: Runs tmux: bind-key (x2), set-hook -g (x2), set-hook -gu (x1), set-option -g automatic-rename-format, and optionally spawns the backgrounded installer. Reads several @wrangler-* options.
edge_cases: Key/focus-key/auto-install options read with `show-option -gqv` (quiet: empty when unset), then defaulted (Tab / a). automatic-rename-format read with `-gv` (NON-quiet).
auto-install-hooks truthy set is exactly {on,1,yes,true}; anything else (incl unset/empty) does not install.
Installer is launched with `run-shell -b` (backgrounded) so plugin load never blocks on config writes; idempotency makes firing every load harmless.
automatic-rename-format guard is a substring test on '@wrangler_sidebar' — do NOT double-wrap if already patched (idempotent across reloads).
If automatic-rename-format were unset the wrap would embed an empty fallback; in practice tmux always has a default so fmt is non-empty. Preserve the raw wrap regardless.
The legacy `set-hook -gu session-window-changed` cleanup must still be emitted (removes a hook installed by older releases).

The after-new-window / after-break-pane hook bodies invoke `spawn --if-active`; in bash they are single-quoted with $CURRENT_DIR interpolated (a path containing a single quote would break the hook — a latent quoting weakness to fix, not replicate, in the port).
Bindings are in the prefix key table (tmux `bind-key` default table), matching current behavior.

functions.name: spawn
functions.signature: fn spawn(win: Option<&str>, if_active: bool) -> Result<()>
functions.behavior: Port of spawn.sh: create one sidebar pane in a window unless it already has one. Resolves the target window id (given arg, else current `#{window_id}`). If if_active, first checks the whole SESSION for any existing sidebar pane (@wrangler_sidebar==1) and exits as a no-op if none (so auto-spawn only happens when the sidebar is toggled on). If the TARGET window already has a sidebar pane, exit no-op. Otherwise read @wrangler-width (default 32) and split a new left-hand, full-height, non-focused pane of that width running the sidebar/daemon; then tag the new pane with pane option @wrangler_sidebar 1.
functions.side_effects: Runs tmux: list-panes probes, split-window (launches the daemon process), set-option -p @wrangler_sidebar 1. Reads @wrangler-width. set -euo pipefail semantics: any tmux failure aborts.
edge_cases: Sidebar detection is on the @wrangler_sidebar PANE OPTION equal to '1' (never the pane command). if-active/session check uses `list-panes -s` (session-wide); the target-window guard uses `list-panes -t win` (that window only).

Original uses `grep -q 1` on a single-field format (@wrangler_sidebar column is '1' or empty) — safe because the field is only ever 1/empty; the port should compare the field == "1" rather than a loose substring.
--if-active shifts the flag off argv, then an optional window id positional follows; port maps to (if_active flag, optional window arg).

Split flags: `-d` (don't switch to it), `-f` (full window height, not just the source pane), `-h` (horizontal split = side-by-side), `-b` (place BEFORE = left), `-l <width>` (size in columns). Reproduce all five semantics.
@wrangler-width is the CONFIGURED default column count (option), distinct from the runtime shared `width` STATE FILE managed by the width module. Default 32.
There is a race window between pane creation and tagging it @wrangler_sidebar 1 (the daemon's own dedup/self-exit handles a double-spawn); the tag is applied by pane id captured from split-window -P.
In the port, the split runs the daemon binary (replacing `python3 sidebar.py`); the command must live inside the pane and read $TMUX_PANE (see `daemon` dep).

functions.name: toggle
functions.behavior: Port of toggle.sh: the on/off switch. Enumerate session-wide sidebar panes (`list-panes -s`, @wrangler_sidebar==1). If any exist, kill every one of them (ignoring per-pane kill errors) and return. Otherwise (turning on): delete the shared `width` STATE FILE, then for EVERY window in the session (`list-windows`) call spawn(window) with NO --if-active (unconditional spawn).
functions.side_effects: Runs tmux: list-panes, kill-pane (x N), list-windows, and spawn per window (which splits panes). Deletes the width state file under $XDG_STATE_HOME (default ~/.local/state)/tmux-agent-wrangler/width. set -euo pipefail.
edge_cases: kill-pane errors are swallowed (`|| true`) to tolerate races (e.g. a pane already gone). Reproduce best-effort kill.

Turning on removes the width state file FIRST so a fresh toggle starts from the configured default width rather than a stale shared width; deletion is `rm -f` (missing file is fine). This is a cross-module touch of the `width` file — prefer routing through the width module.
Spawns via the unconditional spawn path (no if-active gate) — every window gets a sidebar regardless of current session sidebar state.
Sidebar set built with `list-panes -s -F '#{pane_id} #{@wrangler_sidebar}'` filtered by awk '$2==1'; the port should filter panes whose @wrangler_sidebar option is exactly '1'.
State-dir base: $XDG_STATE_HOME if set else $HOME/.local/state, then /tmux-agent-wrangler/width. Match the resolution used everywhere else.

functions.name: focus
functions.behavior: Port of focus.sh: give keyboard focus to the CURRENT window's sidebar pane if it has one; no-op otherwise. Finds the first pane in the current window with @wrangler_sidebar==1, selects it, then sends C-l to that pane to force an immediate repaint (the blocking read would otherwise wait on the 1s poll before the focus highlight appears).
functions.side_effects: Runs tmux: list-panes (current window), select-pane, send-keys C-l. No-op (no writes) when the current window has no sidebar.
edge_cases: Uses CURRENT-window `list-panes` (no -s), and takes the FIRST match only (awk '{print; exit}'). Contrast toggle/spawn which are session-wide. Preserve the current-window, first-match scope.
Never spawns a sidebar — a window without one is a pure no-op (this is why focus is separate from toggle).

The C-l nudge is load-bearing: select-pane delivers no input to the pane, so without it the highlight would lag until the next poll. The daemon treats C-l as a redraw trigger. Keep sending C-l after select-pane.
Detection again keys on the @wrangler_sidebar pane option == '1', not the pane command.

parity_risks: Shell quoting: hook_command must reproduce Python shlex.quote byte-for-byte (unquoted for the safe charset [A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-], else single-quoted with each embedded ' rendered as '\''; empty -> ''). Divergence changes emitted command strings and breaks install idempotency / clean upgrades.

JSON output parity: must preserve object key INSERTION order (ordered map), 2-space indent, ensure_ascii-style \uXXXX escaping of all non-ASCII (serde_json does NOT do this by default), no trailing whitespace, and exactly one trailing newline. Any of these differing produces spurious config diffs.

claude vs copilot structural asymmetry: claude nests a group's actions under one 'hooks' array with an optional leading 'matcher' key; copilot FLATTENS to one {type, matcher?, bash} entry per action. Key ordering within each object is fixed and must be reproduced.

Group replacement invariant: on claude merge, a user's existing hook group is dropped ENTIRELY if any hook in it matches is_wrangler_command (loose \bagent-hook\.sh\b.*\b<agent>\b regex, agent re-escaped). Wrangler groups are re-appended AFTER surviving user groups, in manifest order. This all-or-nothing filtering plus append order is the idempotency contract.
Sticky/side-effecting backup: install_claude rewrites <target>.wrangler.bak on EVERY run while the target exists (install and uninstall alike); copilot has no backup. Don't make it one-time.

File-mode rules differ by format and existence: preserve existing st_mode & 0o777; new claude file = 0o600, new copilot file = 0o644. atomic_write must chmod the temp before the same-directory rename (no umask leakage, no cross-fs temp).

Malformed-input handling: blank/whitespace/missing settings.json -> {}; non-object top level -> hard error; non-dict data['hooks'] -> silently dropped; empty event array -> a real empty group. Preserve each branch exactly (fail-loud where Python does).
groups() shape detection keys only on value[0] being a dict, and object form does g['actions'] (KeyError if missing) — reproduce the fail-on-missing-actions behavior rather than silently defaulting.

CLI arg parsing: last of all|claude|copilot wins; -h/--help returns 0 immediately; unknown arg -> stderr + exit 2; unknown spec.format currently KeyError-crashes (decide whether to reproduce or harden).
Manifest ordering: agent iteration order (the 'all' selector) and per-agent event order come from JSON insertion order and drive output order — must be order-preserving end to end.
@wrangler_sidebar pane option (== '1') is the SOLE source of truth for 'is this a sidebar' — never infer from the pane command anywhere (spawn/toggle/focus/init all rely on this).

Scope asymmetry across the three tmux commands: toggle and spawn-if-active probe SESSION-wide (-s); focus and spawn's target-window guard probe the CURRENT/target window only. Getting the scope wrong changes toggling/focus semantics.

tmux option read flags: keys/auto-install use -gqv (quiet, empty-when-unset then defaulted: Tab / a / off, width 32); automatic-rename-format uses -gv (non-quiet). Defaults must be applied in code, not assumed present.

automatic-rename-format patch is guarded by a substring check on '@wrangler_sidebar' and must stay idempotent (no double-wrapping across repeated plugin loads); and the legacy `set-hook -gu session-window-changed` cleanup must still be emitted.

toggle deletes the shared width state file before spawning (fresh start from configured default) — a cross-module write into `width` territory; route through the width module rather than duplicating the $XDG_STATE_HOME/tmux-agent-wrangler/width path.

focus's post-select C-l nudge and spawn's split flag set (-d -f -h -b -l) are behaviorally load-bearing; dropping the nudge lags the highlight to the poll, and changing split flags relocates/resizes the sidebar.
Backgrounded installer on load (run-shell -b) means installer failures are invisible and must remain non-fatal to plugin init; keep exit codes from install_hooks_main from aborting init.

hook path resolution: HOOK is realpath-resolved (symlinks followed) so the emitted command is stable; the port must resolve the hook subcommand/binary path deterministically (dep: hook), and the literal token 'agent-hook.sh' embedded in is_wrangler_command must match whatever the hook is actually invoked as while still recognising legacy installed entries.
